skills.description: Audit a team's AI usage and spend — which team, which task type and which model the money goes to, how much a cheaper model actually saves, how much capability it costs, and at what volume self-hosting breaks even. Use when the user says "AI costs are too high", "audit our token spend", "LLM bill analysis", "how much did we spend on API calls", "Claude Code billing", "OpenRouter usage export", "compare model pricing", "will a cheaper model hurt quality", "is self-hosting worth it", "cut AI costs", "cost per task". Capabilities: (1) three data sources with a minimum column set — gateway logs (LiteLLM / Helicone / self-built), vendor billing exports, OpenRouter activity export (2) normalization that reconciles cache hits, batch discounts, free credits, and subscription-plus-metered billing into one basis (3) four-dimension cost split across team, project, task type and model, with the top spenders named (4) four unit-economics metrics: cost per task, per pull request, per active user, per thousand lines of code (5) model-switch simulation by capability tier and unit price, including the share of output that needs human review (6) self-hosting TCO: GPU rental or depreciation plus utilization plus ops, turned into a break-even monthly token volume (7) an optimization list sorted by ROI and three cost-reduction plans (conservative / balanced / aggressive) with a staged migration path (8) scripts/cost_audit.py: one command for totals, splits, cache hit rate, switch comparison and self-host break-even. Do not trigger for: wanting a vendor pricing page or a model leaderboard; benchmarking model quality itself; optimizing non-AI cloud spend (EC2, storage, egress); formal accounting treatment.
